present-tense-forms-01-007.note: With a date, a native speaker drops the article: 'Natale è il venticinque dicembre.' 'Il Natale' is the generic/festive use ('Il Natale si passa in famiglia'). Not wrong, but less natural than it should be for a model sentence. Suggested tl/q: 'Natale ___ il venticinque dicembre.'

ce-or-e-01-002.note: 'su questo piano' copies English 'on this floor'. Standard Italian says 'a questo piano': 'Scusi, c'è un distributore di caffè a questo piano?'

ce-or-e-01-009.note: The why says 'fa belongs to the weather only'. That is false: fa piacere, fa bene, fa male are everyday Italian, and item 025 of this same batch says 'fa male means it hurts'. Fix the why, e.g.: 'English it has no Italian counterpart: è difficile + infinitive. C'è would mean there is, and fare does not go with difficile.' The keyed answer and the sentence are fine.

ce-or-e-01-030.note: The why says 'fare is used only with caldo, freddo and tempo'. False: fa fresco, fa bello, fa brutto, fa buio are standard. Fix: 'Neve is a noun, so the pattern is c'è molta neve; fare goes with weather words such as caldo, freddo, fresco or bel tempo, not with a noun like neve.' The item itself is correct.

ce-or-e-01-033.note: Marked lvl 1, but it has 13 words and three clauses ('Sono già le otto meno dieci, è tardi: devo correre al lavoro'). The profile's level 1 is one clause of 4 to 9 words. Make it lvl 2, or shorten it to 'È tardi, devo correre al lavoro.'

ce-or-e-01-046.note: The why says 'Fare takes only caldo, freddo and tempo for the weather'. False: fa fresco, fa bello, fa brutto, fa buio. The judgement itself is right ('fa nuvoloso' is wrong, 'è nuvoloso' is right). Fix the why: 'Nuvoloso is an adjective, so it goes with è: è nuvoloso. Fare does not take nuvoloso.'

ce-or-e-01-049.note: Item-design defect, not an error in the Italian. The extra tile 'molto' cannot be used at all, because 'molta fame' is a single tile, so the learner never makes the molto/molta choice the why describes. Split the tiles ('ho', 'molta', 'fame', ...), keeping 'molto' as the extra, or drop the extra. The tl and the alts are fine.

present-tense-forms.note: 'The loro form follows the vowel of io, not of lui: parlano, but scrivono and dormono' is false: io is parlo, with -o, yet loro is parlano. The real rule is that -are verbs take -ano and -ere/-ire verbs take -ono. The stress part (PARlano, SCRIvono) is correct.

'a short io form' does not fit faccio, and 'Noi and voi are built on the infinitive stem' does not fit facciamo or sappiamo (the note half-admits this). Say instead: tu in -ai, lui in -a, loro in -anno; voi regular (andate, fate, date, state, sapete); noi andiamo, facciamo, diamo, stiamo, sappiamo.
'Avete tempo domani sera, se vi chiamo?' sounds awkward. More natural: 'Se vi chiamo domani sera, avete tempo?' or 'Avete tempo domani sera? Vi chiamo.'
'io fo' is listed as a regularised error, but it is a real Tuscan and literary form of faccio. Replace it with a true learner error such as 'io faco' or 'loro fano'.

'noi is plain too (finiamo, usciamo, veniamo), except possiamo, vogliamo, dobbiamo' leaves out facciamo, sappiamo, diciamo, siamo and abbiamo, so a learner who follows it would write *faciamo or *sapiamo. Limit the claim to -isc- and to the esc-/veng- stems, or list the noi exceptions.

ce-or-e.note: 'After dove only è / sono are possible ... Dove c'è Maria is not Italian.' The first half is false: 'Scusi, dove c'è una farmacia?' and 'Sai dove c'è un bancomat?' are everyday standard Italian (they ask where there is one). Only a known, definite subject rules out c'è: dov'è Maria, dov'è la farmacia. Restate the rule: with a known subject, dove + è/sono; dove c'è + an indefinite new thing is fine.
'After dove always è or sono' is false for the same reason (dove c'è una farmacia?). Say: 'Dove + a known thing or person: dov'è, dove sono.'

'fa takes only caldo, freddo and tempo' is false: fa fresco, fa bello, fa brutto, fa buio, fa freddino. Say: 'fa takes caldo, freddo, fresco, bello/brutto, bel/brutto tempo, never a noun like sole or vento.' Items 030 and 046 repeat the false wording.

patterns: Over-absolute rules in whys and guides that are false at the edges: 'fa only with caldo, freddo, tempo' (ce-or-e 009, 030, 046, guide rules[8].note), 'after dove only è/sono' (guide rules[2].note, cheat[2]), 'short io form / noi on infinitive stem' and 'loro follows the vowel of io' (present-tense guide).
Level-1 items over the profile's one-clause, 4 to 9 word limit (ce-or-e 033 is the clearest; 012, 038, 039 and 045 also have two clauses, as does present-tense 009). Re-level them or shorten them.
Small calques or less natural choices in otherwise correct sentences ('su questo piano', 'Il Natale è il venticinque dicembre', 'Avete tempo domani sera, se vi chiamo?').
Tile design where the extra distractor tile cannot replace anything, because the target form is fused into a larger tile (ce-or-e 049).
